projects.title: MCP Apps to GA
projects.summary: Agent tool UIs built once and rendered in any MCP host, from my RFC to GA in about two months.
highlights: Pitched it, wrote the RFC, and owned it through GA
Shipped custom UI across the dbt platform, VS Code, and Claude Desktop
Other teams now build their own apps on the same pipeline

details.overview: Every rich tool result in dbt's AI surfaces, like lineage graphs and query results, was rebuilt separately for each surface. MCP Apps let a tool ship its own UI once and render it anywhere that speaks the protocol. The idea had been deferred at a team offsite; I kept pushing for it, wrote the RFC, prototyped three architectures in about two weeks, and led it to GA. The catch: dbt's web copilot doesn't speak MCP, so I built a renderer and a server-side resolver that bridge tool results into sandboxed app iframes.
details.role: Lead and RFC author: architecture, the MCP apps package, host renderer, resolver, and the Insight app.
outcomes: RFC to GA in about two months; the first app (a lineage viewer) reached production a month after the RFC
Replaced a fragile iframe handshake with a stateless result handover so apps render behind enterprise browser-security extensions
Insight app (chart, table, and SQL views of agent query results) went GA in August 2026
A teammate built a third app, agent-authored reports, on the same resolver and bundle pipeline

projects.title: Insights Analysis Agent
projects.summary: dbt's conversational analysis agent, moved from request/response to a streaming LangGraph UI and shipped to GA.
highlights: Frontend owner of the agent chat UI through GA
Migrated to streaming with incremental tool-call rendering
Ran the external beta release and post-bug-bash hardening

details.overview: The Insights Copilot used a request/response API, so users stared at "Thinking…" with no sense of progress. As the backend moved to a streaming LangGraph endpoint, I reworked the chat so streamed chunks become the same messages our tool-call renderers already understood. The new path shipped as versioned components, so the old one could be removed later without touching Copilot in other apps. Along the way I added reasoning sections that grow as the agent thinks, @-mentions that pass models and files to the agent as context, and agent-run SQL that fills the query editor and results.
details.role: Frontend owner: streaming chat architecture, message renderers, release gating.
outcomes: Reached full feature parity with the previous agent, then external beta in January 2026 and GA
A fail-closed feature gate moved existing users to the new agent without disruption
Shipped fixes for every medium-to-critical issue from the pre-launch bug bash
Built a standalone test bed to iterate against a live backend without loading the full app

projects.title: Dev-Agent Workspace
projects.summary: A full-screen workspace for reviewing AI code edits, with side-by-side diffs and visual DAG diffs of every change.
highlights: Frontend lead: wrote the eng plan, ran the kickoff, built most of it
Split-pane review of agent edits with a code ⇄ Canvas toggle
Visual before/after DAG diffs for SQL changes

details.overview: The dev agent's changes used to show up as small diff cards in the chat, and nothing showed what a SQL change did structurally. I took over the effort, re-planned it after my first prototype pointed the wrong way, and built a resizable side pane next to the chat: full-height diffs, chat history that shows each edit as it was at that point in the conversation, and a toggle that renders the change as a before/after DAG in Canvas, dbt's visual SQL editor.
details.role: Frontend lead: eng plan, split-pane shell, DAG diff components, telemetry, release flags.
outcomes: Launched internally in May 2026 as the default full-screen experience; public preview in July
Recovered from a launch incident with a lazy-loaded, flag-gated re-land the day after the revert
Instrumented the review flow end to end with product telemetry
Product asked to reuse the code/Canvas toggle in other parts of the platform

projects.title: React 19 + Compiler Migration
projects.summary: Led the React 19 + Compiler migration across six repos, cutting render time by ~54%.
highlights: React rendering time cut by ~54% with a compiled component library
Key contributor to unifying five frontend apps into one monorepo
CDN-split the editor core to fix chronic CI failures

details.overview: dbt's frontends ran a mix of React 18 and 19, so the shared packages had to support both, and that blocked consolidating into a monorepo. I took the shared component library and app navigation to React 19 and rolled it out across six repos. Then I went past the plan's stretch goal: a compiled build of the component library (plus a legacy build so other apps kept working), compiler lint rules, and a forms overhaul that keeps form state reactive under the compiler. Separately, I moved the heavyweight Monaco/VS Code editor core out to a CDN so the editor app stopped toppling CI.
details.role: Migration lead: planning, rollout across six repos, perf measurement, adoption docs.
outcomes: ~54% less React rendering time from the compiled component library
Fixed a long-standing forms bug while making forms compiler-safe
Cleared the biggest unknown for moving the main app into the monorepo
Chronic editor-related CI failures eliminated via the CDN split

projects.title: Design Token Pipeline
projects.summary: A Figma-to-code design token pipeline that shipped dark mode company-wide and turned the brand refresh into a one-package change.
highlights: Lead architect for the Figma → npm token pipeline
Shipped dark mode across six repositories
Built a lint plugin and ran an org-wide token mob to drive adoption

details.overview: Designers had light and dark variables in Figma, but code used raw Tailwind colors, so there was no way to theme the product. I built a token package that turns the Figma variable export into CSS variables and Tailwind config, layered primitive → alias → semantic, with light and dark in one file. Then I pushed it well past the planned ~10% adoption: an ESLint plugin that flags raw colors, a migration guide and office hours, a company-wide Design Token Mob, a theme preference stored per user, and a phased dark-mode rollout to customers.
details.role: Lead and sole engineer on the pipeline; co-led the rollout with design.
outcomes: Dark mode shipped to every customer tier in early 2025
One token source used across six repositories
The 2025 brand refresh became a color change in a single package
The token mob converted thousands of Tailwind classes to tokens
